title: Fawlty Towers – The Play
blurb: Stage adaptation of the classic John Cleese sitcom plays a six-day run at the Grand Canal Dock theatre.

title: Annie the Musical
blurb: The family-favourite musical about the plucky Depression-era orphan opens its Dublin week during the window.

title: The Brightening Air by Conor McPherson
blurb: McPherson directs his own award-winning play about siblings in a 1980s rural Irish homestead, a Gate presentation of the Old Vic production.

title: Riverdance 30 – The New Generation
blurb: The 30th-anniversary edition of the Irish dance phenomenon runs all summer at its home theatre, with matinee and evening shows most days.

title: Gallagher Dublin Horse Show
blurb: Five-day showjumping spectacular with the 100th Aga Khan Nations' Cup (Aug 7), the Puissance (Aug 8), a €1m Grand Prix (Aug 9), Shetland Pony Grand National and a family zone; kids under 4 free.

title: Rembrandt to Matisse – A Celebration of European Prints and Drawings
blurb: Admission-free exhibition of around fifty of the Gallery's finest European works on paper, running 27 June to 8 November 2026.

title: Common Ground: Ireland and the EU
blurb: New multimedia exhibition timed to Ireland's EU presidency, exploring Irish influence in Europe, on show 1 July to 31 December 2026.

title: Dublin by Dusk: Late Opening at EPIC
blurb: EPIC stays open late on Thursday 30 July as part of the city-wide Dublin by Dusk initiative.

title: Rainforest Takeover – August Bank Holiday Weekend
blurb: Three days of rainforest-themed activities across the zoo, including a self-guided Rainforest Ranger Trail with a VIP experience prize for kids.

title: Making A Show of Myself
blurb: Moth Grand Slam champion Mary Kate O Flanagan performs six true stories in a solo show fresh from an off-Broadway run.

title: Lost the Plot: An Improvised Musical
blurb: One-night fully improvised musical where every song and plot twist is invented live on the spot.

title: Underdog: The Other Other Brontë
blurb: Two-night staging following Charlotte Brontë's rise to fame and the rivalry among the Brontë sisters.

title: Dublin Literary Pub Crawl
venue: The Duke Pub, 9 Duke Street (start point)
blurb: Actor-led nightly summer walk through four historic pubs and Trinity College, performing Joyce, Beckett, Wilde and Behan along the way.

title: Howth Market
blurb: Up to 25 stalls of fresh food, artisan produce and crafts by the harbour, open Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays 9am-6pm (incl. Mon 3 Aug).

title: People's Park Market
blurb: Sunday food and craft market (11am-4pm) in a Victorian seaside park with a playground and tearoom, near the DART.

title: GAZE International LGBTQIA Film Festival
venue: Light House Cinema & Irish Film Institute
blurb: Ireland's long-running queer film festival, founded in 1992, screens features and shorts across two city cinemas.

title: A New Form of Beauty: Dublin Youth Culture, Street Style and Subculture 1960s-1990s
venue: National Museum of Ireland – Decorative Arts & History, Collins Barracks
blurb: Photographic exhibition of Dublin street style and subcultures from the 1960s to 1990s, in its final month at Collins Barracks.

title: Free August Tours of the Archaeology Collection
venue: National Museum of Ireland – Archaeology, Kildare Street
blurb: Guide-led free tours of the archaeology collection run throughout August; no booking, first come first served, kids welcome with an adult.

title: Summer in Dublin – Free Weekend Street Events
blurb: Dublin City Council's free weekend series turns Parliament Street into a family playground with street performers, interactive shows and workshops.

title: Historical Walking Tours of Dublin (The Original Tour)
blurb: Two-hour tour led by history professionals covering the English conquest through the peace process, running daily in season since 1986.
